facts.title: Regulator and legal basis
facts.body: The NDA registers human medicines under the National Drug Policy and Authority Act (Cap. 206), being replaced by the National Drug and Health Products Authority Act, 2026. The National Drug Register (over 4,000 human, veterinary and public-health products) is public: a search on the NDA site and monthly PDF lists per category. Uganda is a WHO Maturity Level 3 regulator and takes part in the East African Community joint assessment.

facts.title: A local technical representative
facts.body: A foreign licence holder appoints a local technical representative licensed by the NDA in Uganda, named on the register with the licence holder; the representative files, answers queries and handles pharmacovigilance and recalls.

facts.title: 90-day verification route; 8 to 18 months otherwise
facts.body: The NDA runs a verification (reliance) review with a 90-day target for products approved by stringent regulators or WHO prequalified, abridged reviews and a priority track. Service providers report 8 to 12 months for an abridged generic, 12 to 18 months for a full review and 4 to 6 months for WHO-prequalified products. The NDA's service delivery timelines were revised in July 2024.

facts.title: NDA GMP inspection of the foreign site
facts.body: Each foreign manufacturing site is inspected by the NDA (or recognised through EAC joint inspections, PIC/S or WHO prequalification) before registration; the inspection is charged separately and the applicant pays travel. Budget USD 4,000 to 15,000 per site plus expenses.

facts.title: Registration fees
facts.body: Registration fees are set per product in the NDA fees schedule: about USD 500 per product for registration (older guides) with ranges of USD 300 to 1,200 reported by service providers, plus annual retention and the separate GMP inspection fee. Confirm the current schedule with the NDA.

facts.title: CTD in the EAC format
facts.body: The dossier follows the East African Community CTD (modules 1 to 5) in English, with GMP evidence, a certificate of pharmaceutical product, bioequivalence for multisource oral solid forms, stability for zone IVb and samples for the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory.

facts.title: Duty-free and VAT-exempt medicines
facts.body: Medicines enter at 0% under the East African Community Common External Tariff and are exempt from VAT under the VAT Act (with the Uganda Revenue Authority listing the covered items); each shipment needs an NDA import verification.

facts.title: Essential list 2023, public procurement through NMS
facts.body: The Essential Medicines and Health Supplies List of Uganda (EMHSLU 2023) sets levels of use (HC1 to NR) and a vital/essential/necessary class; National Medical Stores buys for public facilities and the Joint Medical Store for faith-based ones.

routes.label: Full review (NDA)
routes.description: EAC CTD through a local technical representative, NDA GMP inspection of the site, samples to the national laboratory. 12 to 18 months in practice; fee per product plus the inspection.

routes.label: Verification review (stringent approval or WHO prequalification)
routes.description: For products approved by a stringent regulator or WHO prequalified: verification review with a 90-day target, GMP recognised; 4 to 6 months in practice.

routes.label: EAC joint assessment
routes.description: One dossier assessed jointly by the EAC regulators (Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan), then national registration in each; Uganda recognises the joint outcome.
